commit_message:
avcodec/sanm: better frame size detection for old codecs

The size of the video frame (FOBJ) of the old codecs (ANIMv0/1/2) can
very reliably be determined:
- ANIMv0/1 (=Rebel Assault 1) uses a 384x242 internal buffer for
  everything.  The codec parameters only describe the size and offset
  of the specific FOBJ on that buffer.
- ANIMv2 titles usually use one of the fullscreen codecs (37/47/48)
  as first FOBJ, and their dimensions can generally be trusted.
- RA2 uses 424x260 as internal buffer, use that if encountered:
  08PLAY.SAN does not use codec37 so we need to guess using the
  codec coordinates.
- ignore sizes smaller than 2x2 or larger than 800x600.
- some game videos have an initial fobj with either 1x1 or -1x-1
  pixels in size, ignore them with a warning (Full Throttle
  and the Rebel Assault 2 xxRETRY.SAN videos).

Once a known/valid dimension set has been discovered, use it and
don't change it for subsequent FOBJs, rather clamp the large frame
to the determined dimensions.

Tested with RA1, RA2, Full Throttle, Dig, Outlaws, SotE and MotS
videos.

Signed-off-by: Manuel Lauss <manuel.lauss@gmail.com>

fix_commit.message: avcodec/sanm: Check w, h for subversion < 2
fix_commit.author: Michael Niedermayer

findings.title: Missing bounds check for w/h against fixed 384x242 internal buffer (subversion < 2 / Rebel Assault 1)
findings.message: In process_frame_obj(), when ctx->subversion < 2 (Rebel Assault 1 ANIMv0/1 files), the internal frame buffer dimensions are hard-coded to xres=384, yres=242, and ctx->have_dimensions is set to 1 without validating that the FOBJ's own w/h (and implicitly left/top placement) fit within this 384x242 buffer. The earlier sanity check only enforces 1 <= w <= 800 and 1 <= h <= 600, which is far larger than 384x242. As a result, a crafted SANM/ANIM file can supply w/h values up to 800x600 while ctx->subversion < 2, causing the decoder to believe the frame fits in the 384x242 buffer (init_sizes/init_buffers are sized to 384x242) while subsequent decode routines write/read using the attacker supplied larger w/h and left/top offsets, leading to out-of-bounds array access on the small fixed-size buffer.
findings.suggestion: When ctx->subversion < 2, validate that the parsed w and h do not exceed the fixed internal buffer size (384x242) before accepting the dimensions and marking ctx->have_dimensions = 1. If w or h exceed the fixed bounds, return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA instead of proceeding.

ground_truth.root_cause: The frame-size detection logic added in commit 93b0ca26ac ("better frame size detection for old codecs") assumes that for old ANIMv0/1 (subversion < 2) files the internal frame is always exactly 384x242, and unconditionally trusts this fixed size without cross-checking it against the actually parsed FOBJ w/h fields, which are only bounded by a much looser generic check (w<=800, h<=600). This allows fields not fitting the assumed fixed buffer to pass through.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Missing bounds check for w/h against fixed 384x242 internal buffer (subversion < 2 / Rebel Assault 1)
